## A macro error inside a function body is never reported: `fn main() { compile_error!("msg"); }` builds silently

blaze-diagnostics tests::items::macros::compile_error_is_an_error_at_the_call has printed nothing since round 12 (BUILTINS_CORE fixture: `compile_error` is the `#[rustc_builtin_macro]` of core's prelude, resolved). rustc: error "msg" at the call (line 2). The parse error of an expansion in a body is lost the same way (tests::items::macros::an_expansion_that_ends_inside_an_expression_says_so_at_its_last_token: only 01380's borrowck leak is printed, not "macro expansion ends with an incomplete expression"). The route: hir reports body macro errors from `BodySourceMap::macro_calls()` (hir/src/diagnostics.rs:3240, then `collect_macro_call` at 2160), which reads `expansions` (hir-def/src/expr_store/source_map.rs:1014). Those are pushed only under `self.store.record` (expr_store/lower.rs:3034, 3005), and `record` is cleared at expr_store.rs:839. Please check that the source map hir walks there is built with `record` on for statement-position calls (`collect_macro_as_stmt`, lower.rs:3068). Otherwise, report from `ExpressionStore::macro_calls()`, which is always kept. Item-level `compile_error!` goes through `DefDiagnosticKind::MacroError` and works. Program impact: `compile_error!` under a `cfg`-selected branch in a fn body (common in real crates) is ignored.
